title: Identification of key genes as potential diagnostic and therapeutic targets for comorbidity of myasthenia gravis and COVID-19.
authors: Huang, Liyan; Zuo, Yao; Yang, Hui; He, Xiaofang; Zhang, Lin
one_liner_zh: 该文通过差异表达分析筛选重症肌无力与COVID-19共病关键基因，并预测转录因子及分子对接，但核心是疾病标志物而非蛋白质-DNA互作机制研究，方法上仅涉及简单对接，与本课题关联较弱。
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Myasthenia gravis (MG) is a chronic autoimmune neuromuscular disorder. Coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) has a significant impact on the health and quality of life of MG patients and may even trigger the onset of MG in some cases. With the worldwide development of the COVID-19 vaccination, several new-onset MG cases and exacerbations following the COVID-19 vaccines have been acknowledged. The potential link between myasthenia gravis (MG) and COVID-19 has prompted the need for further investigation into the underlying molecular mechanism. METHODS AND RESULTS: The differential expression analysis identified six differentially expressed genes (DEGs) shared by myasthenia gravis (MG) and COVID-19, namely SAMD9, PLEK, GZMB, JUNB, NR4A1, and NR1D1. The relationship between the six common genes and immune cells was investigated in the COVID-19 dataset. The predictive value of the shared genes was assessed and a nomogram was constructed using machine learning algorithms. The regulatory miRNAs, transcription factors and small molecular drugs were predicted, and the molecular docking was carried out by AutoDock. DISCUSSION: We have identified six common DEGs of MG and COVID-19 and explored their immunological effects and regulatory mechanisms. The result may provide new insights for further mechanism research.
abstract_zh: 引言：重症肌无力（MG）是一种慢性自身免疫性神经肌肉疾病。2019冠状病毒病（COVID-19）对MG患者的健康和生命质量产生显著影响，甚至在某些情况下可能诱发MG的发病。随着全球范围内COVID-19疫苗接种的推进，已有若干接种后新发MG病例及病情加重的情况被确认。重症肌无力（MG）与COVID-19之间的潜在关联促使有必要进一步探究其潜在的分子机制。方法与结果：差异表达分析识别出重症肌无力（MG）与COVID-19共有的六个差异表达基因（DEGs），即SAMD9、PLEK、GZMB、JUNB、NR4A1和NR1D1。在COVID-19数据集中研究了这六个共有基因与免疫细胞之间的关系。评估了共有基因的预测价值，并利用机器学习算法构建了列线图。预测了调控性miRNA、转录因子及小分子药物，并通过AutoDock进行了分子对接。讨论：我们识别出MG与COVID-19的六个共有DEGs，并探讨了它们的免疫效应及调控机制。该结果可能为进一步的机制研究提供新的见解。
